title: Parsing CSV held in a string: literal data needs I() in readr 2.2, and type guessing loses identifiers
source_relation: original construction on the readr 2.2.0 literal-data deprecation; closest registry families are deprecated-parameter handling and explicit-loss parsing
difficulty_hypothesis: Widely taught read_csv(text_string) now warns in readr 2.2.0 (literal data must be wrapped in I()); type guessing silently turns '007' into 7 and invalid timestamps into guesses; counting parse problems requires telling missing values from unparseable ones.

mcp_relevance.rationale: The literal-data change is a very recent readr release note that most training material predates; knowing the installed readr's behaviour requires version-specific documentation. The warning text itself shows the fix, and base R read.csv(text=) avoids the issue altogether.
mcp_relevance.information_need: How the installed readr expects in-memory CSV text to be passed, and how to control column types.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: partly: the warning message prints the I() fix; base R is a complete fallback

pinned_evidence.observed: read_csv('a,b\n1,2') warns: The `file` argument of `read_csv()` should use `I()` for literal data as of readr 2.2.0
pinned_evidence.oracle: base R read.csv(text=, colClasses = 'character') with explicit strptime/as.numeric conversion; any warning fails
